title: operand-level-fusion-strategies-paged-kv-notes
content:
Context:
This doc collects informal notes and micro-experiment results for a new approach we're calling "operand-level fusion" (OLF) combined with paged-KV prefetch strategies. Goal: reduce per-token cost and tail latency for interactive workloads by fusing small element-wise / shuffle operations into FlashAttention-like kernels and by hiding paged-KV page faults through cooperative prefetching and GPU-side staging.

High-level goals / constraints:
- Target 1: reduce per-token GPU cycles for 2~4k seq chat workloads by 10–25% relative to our current FlashAttention + separate post-processing kernels.
- Target 2: keep 99.9th-latency regression < 10% (compared to baseline with small added prefetch overhead).
- Constraint: support quantized weight formats (4/8-bit) and page-aware KV sequences (paged KV where KV size >> GPU memory).
- Must be compatible with our runtime fallbacks (can fall back to separate kernels).

Summary of idea (TL;DR):
- Instead of only fusing attention + softmax/scale primitives at the block level, implement operand-level fusion where matrix/tile outputs are directly consumed by the next operator without writing back to global memory.
- For paged KV, maintain a small GPU-resident page cache and a cooperative prefetch kernel that runs ahead of token processing, ensuring required KV pages are resident before attention fetches.
- Combine with light-weight per-warp micro-schedulers to overlap prefetch DMA with compute using stream/substream semantics.

Why this differs from prior notes:
- Prior docs focused on macro-level fusion (concatenate multiple ops into one big kernel). OLF focuses on fusing at the operand boundary (producer->consumer) across variable tiling and across quantized conv between ops. That keeps kernel code paths smaller and compositionally reusable.

Design notes: operand-level fusion patterns
- Producers: attention tile (Flash-style SxS partial products), matmul tiles, linear-project tiles (quantized).
- Consumers: layernorm+residual add, activation+quantize, key/value writeback to paged buffer.
- Fusion units: define a small ABI where a producer emits a tile via registers/shared memory and then calls a consumer subroutine (inlined via templated device code). No global store if consumer can consume immediately.

Kernel sketch (pseudo):

// fused producer-consumer tile loop (simplified)
for (tileIdx : tiles) {
  load_tile_A_into_regs(); // can be Q4/Q8 path
  load_tile_B_into_regs();
  compute_partial_C_in_regs(); // warp-level accumulate
  // operand-level handoff (no global write)
  consumer_process_tile_inplace(regs, shared_scratch);
  if (needs_kv_writeback) {
    // write to staged page buffer (coalesced)
    staged_write_page(tileIdx, regs);
  }
}

Key micro-optimizations to explore:
- Avoiding extra copies: prefer register->shared->consumer pipeline, use inline device functions with __restrict__ pointers to avoid needless spills.
- Tiling choices: prefer rectangular tiles that match load/store width of quantized formats (e.g., 128x32) to keep vector loads aligned.
- Loop unrolling size tuned for occupancy vs register pressure. Provide a compile profile step that selects unroll depth to keep per-thread register usage under threshold for target SM (A100/H100).
- Dynamic scratch allocation: small fixed shared memory per CTAs for intermediate reordering before consumer to reduce bank conflicts.

Paged-KV prefetching and staging
- Page model: KV divided into fixed-size pages (e.g., 256kB hot page). Each request references a sequence of pages.
- On CPU side: runtime computes page list for upcoming token horizon (lookahead = N tokens).
- On GPU side: lightweight prefetch kernel maintains a resident page table (RPT) in GPU memory: page id -> GPU buffer pointer / invalid marker.
- Prefetch kernel uses asynchronous P2P / cudaMemcpyAsync from host pinned staging region or GPU-to-GPU UVM copies (for multi-gpu nodes).
- Important invariant: before attention reads KV for token t, all referenced pages must be marked resident in RPT. Prefetch should aim to complete earlier than the compute that consumes it by lookahead tokens.

Prefetching pseudocode (producer-consumer model):
- host: compute page list for batch B, push to prefetch queue (per-stream).
- prefetch kernel (stream S_prefetch): take next page id, if missing in RPT, issue async memcpy from host->GPU buffer; on completion set RPT entry and signal a flag/atomic.
- compute kernel (stream S_compute pinned to same device): when tile needs page p, check RPT flag; if not present and watermark low -> either stall for completion or trigger on-demand blocking upload (rare).

Watermarks and eviction policy:
- Keep pinned resident working set size W (in pages) per model / per-partition. Evict LRU pages when resident > W.
- Define two watermarks: prefetch_high and eviction_low. Prefetching continues until resident_pages >= prefetch_high. Eviction runs when resident_pages > eviction_high. Eviction_low provides hysteresis to avoid frequent thrashing.
- For mixed priority workloads (hosted multi-tenant), allow per-tenant weighted watermarks.

Microbenchmark results (selected):
- Hardware: A100-80GB (PCIe gen4), CUDA 12.1, gcc 11, nvcc flags: -O3 -arch=sm_80. Baseline = FlashAttention + separate postproc kernel.

Experiment A: small-cx (seq=512, batch=8)
- Baseline throughput: 230 tokens/s per GPU
- OLF fused (no paging): 270 tokens/s per GPU (+17%)
- OLF + prefetch staged pages (hot pages residency 40MB): 255 tokens/s per GPU (+11%, slight prefetch overhead for small horizon)

Experiment B: long-cx (seq=2048, batch=4) with paged KV (total KV 12GB)
- Baseline (naive paging with CPU-on-demand copy): 48 tokens/s
- OLF + cooperative prefetch (lookahead=6 tokens): 68 tokens/s (+42%)
- OLF + prefetch + compressed-page (4-bit packed pages) + fused quant-unpack consumer: 82 tokens/s (+71% over baseline)

Notes on measurements:
- 99.9th latency: baseline had large spikes (up to 3x median) due to synchronous host copies. Prefetching reduced spikes significantly but introduced small steady overhead in small-batch workloads. Tunable lookahead mitigates this.
- Memory footprint: OLF increases register/shared memory usage; in extreme unroll variants we saw occupancy drop from 70% -> 42% which hurt small-batch throughput.

Heuristics for runtime selection:
- At model-load time, run a light microprofile pass (100 synthetic tokens) to measure sequence distribution and per-token compute time. Use that to pick fusion config: aggressive (max fusion) vs conservative (split out postproc).
- When paged-KV working set < per-GPU RAM * 0.2, disable prefetch (cost > benefit).
- For high tail-sensitivity customers, pick conservative eviction (bigger W) to avoid faults.

Implementation risks & mitigations:
- Risk: register pressure from fusion causes spills -> net regression. Mitigation: auto-tune unroll/reg limits per-arch and keep a fallback kernel chain path.
- Risk: page thrashing for multi-tenant noisy neighbors. Mitigation: tenant weights + eviction quotas + per-tenant admission control.
- Risk: complex kernel debugging (fused code harder to trace). Mitigation: maintain a debug build that emits per-tile telemetry markers and small deterministic replay harness.

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Explore per-warp small circular buffer in shared memory to implement zero-copy consumer handoff. Microbench for bank conflicts at different tile shapes.
- Test on H100 & RTX-class to confirm register tradeoffs (H100 has larger register file, may favor more aggressive OLF).
- Investigate integrating with existing FlashAttention variant (we've prototyped a "FlashPlus" branch) — measure complexity of merging templates.
- Evaluate prefetch lookahead auto-tuning: can we adapt lookahead based on observed page latencies online? Quick design: exponential moving average of page fetch latency per-page-class and adjust lookahead to target X ms headroom.

Notes-to-self (todo):
- Add small per-kernel telemetry tags that show whether consumer executed inlined or via fallback.
- Add a small fuzz harness to check correctness for quantized fused pipeline (bit-exact vs FP baseline tolerance).
- Open PR for fused op ABI proposal: linked PR above.

Relevant links and references:
- FlashAttention paper + open-source kernels (we use their attention tiling inspiration).
- internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/941 (prototype OLF kernels)
- Jira: SERV-1282 (paged-kv design), SERV-1309 (prefetch infra)

Concluding notes:
- Early results are promising for long-context paged-KV workloads; the biggest wins are when you can both avoid global writes and overlap host/page IO with compute.
- Main engineering effort: robust auto-tuner that keeps register/shared usage in range and a well-tested page resident manager with per-tenant policies.

If you're reviewing: focus on the eviction policy and the register/occupancy tradeoffs — those are the engineering knobs most likely to determine production viability.

-- Marina
